title: The four Uniswap v4 pools apply contradictory outflow policies with nothing in the documents explaining the split
content:
Within one protocol family the exit policy diverges. Uniswap v4 PYUSD/USDS sets outflow "`maxAmount`: 50,000,000, `slope`: 200,000,000 per day" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.11.1.2.4.2) and USDT/USDS the same (.11.2.2.4.2), while USDG/USDS (.11.3.2.4.2) and rlUSD/USDS (.11.4.2.4.2) both state simply "`maxAmount`: Unlimited".

All four are USDS-paired stablecoin pools on the same protocol with the same 0.0005% fee and the same tick-and-slippage construction. Nothing in the four documents distinguishes the pairs in a way that would justify capping withdrawal from two of them.

A capped outflow is defensible for an LP position on general grounds — unwinding returns two assets in a ratio the pool decides, so exiting is a composition change rather than a clean redemption, and pulling liquidity abruptly can worsen the price Spark exits at. But that argument applies equally to all four pools.

So either the two unlimited entries are the outliers and the intended policy is a 50,000,000 cap, or the two capped entries reflect a specific concern about PYUSD and USDT that the Artifact does not record. Combined with the missing `Max tick width` on the same two instances that carry unlimited outflow, the more likely reading is drafting drift rather than deliberate differentiation — which is itself the finding: at this level of the tree, parameter differences between sibling instances cannot be assumed to carry meaning.
description: PYUSD/USDS and USDT/USDS cap outflow at 50,000,000 with a 200,000,000 per day slope, while USDG/USDS and rlUSD/USDS leave outflow Unlimited despite near-identical structure.
